q: Leo wears his red cap to every baseball game. What does Leo wear to baseball games?
why: The story says Leo wears a red cap. The other things are not in the story.
hint: Find the clothing word in the first sentence.

q: A hammerhead shark has a wide, flat head. True or false: its head is shaped like a round ball.
why: The text says wide and flat, which is not round like a ball.
hint: Check the words wide and flat.

q: Ana's puppy ran to the door and wagged its tail when she got home. How did the puppy feel?
why: A wagging tail and running to the door show joy. Sleepy dogs stay still.
hint: What do wagging tails usually show?

q: Put the beach story in order.
opts: Dan filled a bucket with wet sand.
A little tower stood on the beach.
why: The bucket has to be filled and flipped before there is a tower to wash away.
hint: What must happen before the tower can stand?

q: The shark swam fast to catch a fish. Why did the shark swim fast?
why: The story gives the reason right in the first sentence: to catch a fish.
hint: Look for the word 'to' in the sentence.

q: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep, so they do not drift apart. What is this mostly about?
why: Every part of the sentence is about otters holding hands as they sleep. Food and nests are not mentioned.
hint: Ask what most of the sentence tells about.

q: Read: Three whales swam by. Then two more whales joined them. How many whales are there now?
why: Three whales plus two more whales makes five whales.
hint: Add the whales together.

q: A book has a title on its cover. What does the title tell you?
why: The title is the name of the book. It does not tell you the ending or the length.
hint: Think about what you call a book.

q: Sam grabbed his glove and ran to the field. His team was waiting. What will Sam most likely do next?
why: A glove, a field and a waiting team all point to a baseball game.
hint: Use the clues about the glove and the field.

q: The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight bounces off it. True or false: moonlight is really sunlight bouncing off the Moon.
why: The Moon only reflects sunlight, a bit like a mirror does.
hint: Reread the second sentence.

q: Waves rolled onto the sand and gulls called overhead. Dan dug with a shovel. Where is Dan?
why: Waves, sand and gulls are all beach clues.
hint: Which clues name sand and waves?

q: Put these ocean animals in ABC order, first letter first.
why: The first letters c, f, s and w come in that order in the alphabet.
hint: Say the alphabet and find each first letter.

q: Mo found his lost baseball under the bed. He jumped up and shouted, 'Yes!' How did Mo feel?
why: Jumping up and shouting 'Yes!' shows excitement, not fear or sadness.
hint: How do people act when they find something good?

q: A cat has fur. A fish has scales. What does a fish have that a cat does not?
why: The text says fish have scales and cats have fur. A cat does not have scales.
hint: Compare the two sentences.

q: Read: Kai had 4 baseball cards. Dee gave him 3 more. How many cards does Kai have now?
why: Kai had 4 cards and got 3 more, so 4 plus 3 equals 7.
hint: Add the cards Dee gave.

q: A book shows how to make a paper boat, step by step. Why did the author write it?
opts: To tell a funny story about pirates
To show how to make a boat
why: Step-by-step directions are written to teach you how to do something.
hint: What do step-by-step directions help you do?

q: A T. rex had tiny arms but strong legs and a huge head. Which part of a T. rex was tiny?
why: The text says tiny arms. The legs were strong and the head was huge.
hint: Find the word tiny.

q: A glossary is a list of words and what they mean. True or false: a glossary can help you learn a new word.
why: A glossary lists words with their meanings, so it helps with new words.
hint: Think about what the list tells you.

q: A sea star has no brain and no blood. It moves sea water through its body instead. Which of these does a sea star NOT have?
why: The text says no brain and no blood. Sea stars do have a mouth and arms.
hint: Find the word no in the first sentence.

q: Ruby looked through her telescope at the night sky. She saw bright dots far away. What was Ruby looking at?
why: A telescope at night shows faraway bright dots, which are stars.
hint: Where was she looking, and how far away were the dots?

q: The tiny hermit crab was timid. When a big wave came, it hid inside its shell. What does timid mean?
why: The crab hid when the wave came, which shows it is shy and easily scared.
hint: What does hiding tell you about the crab?

q: Jake's team was behind by one run. He took a deep breath, gripped the bat and watched the pitcher closely. What is Jake trying to do?
why: Gripping the bat and watching the pitcher means he is getting ready to hit.
hint: Think about why a batter watches the pitcher.

q: Sharks have skeletons made of cartilage, not bone. Cartilage is the soft, bendy stuff in your ears. True or false: a shark's skeleton is made of cartilage.
why: Sharks have no bones. Their cartilage skeleton bends, like the tip of your ear.
hint: Reread the first sentence.

q: Put the butterfly's life story in order.
opts: A tiny egg sits on a leaf.
A caterpillar hatches and eats leaves.
why: The egg comes first, and the butterfly comes out only after the chrysalis stage.
hint: What is the very first thing in a butterfly's life?

q: Seahorse dads carry the eggs in a pouch on their bellies. The babies pop out when they are ready. What is the main idea?
opts: Seahorses lay eggs on dry land
Baby seahorses eat lots of seaweed
why: Both sentences are about the dad carrying eggs. Land and seaweed are never mentioned.
hint: What do both sentences talk about?

q: Tim's team won the championship. He hugged his teammates and could not stop smiling. How did Tim feel?
why: Hugging and smiling after a win show Tim felt thrilled, which means very happy.
hint: Look at what Tim does with his face.

q: Read: A baseball game has 9 innings. The team has played 4 innings. How many innings are left?
why: 9 innings minus 4 played innings leaves 5 innings.
hint: Subtract the played innings from the total.

q: Because gravity pulls everything toward Earth, a baseball hit high into the air comes back down. What brings the baseball down?
why: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth. Wind can move a ball sideways but does not pull it down.
hint: What force does the first part of the sentence name?

q: Which part of a book lists the chapters and their page numbers?
why: The table of contents shows chapters and pages. A glossary explains words instead.
hint: It is found near the front of the book.

q: The plant on the windowsill drooped because nobody watered it. True or false: the plant drooped because it got too much water.
why: The text says nobody watered it, so it drooped from too little water.
hint: Find the word because and read what follows.

q: The astronaut floated past the window, and her pencil drifted in the air beside her. Where is she most likely?
why: Objects float inside a spacecraft in orbit instead of falling as they would on Earth.
hint: On Earth, a pencil would fall.

q: The dinosaur's footprint was enormous. A whole family could stand inside it. What does enormous mean?
why: If a whole family fits in the footprint, it must be very large.
hint: How big must a footprint be for a family to fit?

q: Put the baseball play in order.
opts: The batter hit a line drive.
The crowd clapped for the out.
why: The pitch starts the play, and the crowd claps only after the catch.
hint: What has to happen before anyone can catch the ball?

q: A writer tells a funny story about a dog who wears sunglasses. Why did the writer most likely write it?
why: Funny stories are written to entertain. Directions and facts are not the goal here.
hint: Is the story meant to teach or to be fun?

q: Whale sharks are huge, but they eat tiny plankton. They swim with their mouths open and filter food from the water. What do whale sharks eat?
why: Size can fool you. The text says this huge shark eats tiny plankton.
hint: Find the food named in the first sentence.

q: Jellyfish have no bones, no brain and no heart. True or false: a jellyfish has a heart.
why: Jellyfish are made mostly of water and have no heart, brain or bones.
hint: Look for the word no in the passage.

q: Orbit means to travel around something. The Moon orbits Earth. What does the Moon do?
why: Orbit means travel around, so the Moon travels around Earth.
hint: Use the meaning the passage gives for orbit.

q: Read: A shark lost 2 teeth while eating lunch and 4 more while eating dinner. New teeth grew in each time. How many teeth did it lose in all?
why: The shark lost 2 and then 4 more, so 2 plus 4 equals 6. Regrowing does not change the count lost.
hint: Add only the teeth that fell out.

q: A dictionary page has the guide words dog and duck. Which word could be found on that page?
why: Door comes after dog and before duck in ABC order, so it fits between the guide words.
hint: Compare the first letters, then the second letters.

q: A frog has smooth, wet skin. A toad has dry, bumpy skin. How is a toad's skin different from a frog's?
why: The toad's skin is dry and bumpy, while the frog's is smooth and wet.
hint: Compare the two skin descriptions.

q: The explorer was parched after hours in the hot desert. She gulped down a whole bottle of water. What does parched mean?
why: Gulping a whole bottle of water is a clue: parched means very thirsty.
hint: Why would someone gulp water?

q: The coach looked at the dark clouds, then at the scoreboard. 'Let's finish quickly before the rain,' she said. What is she worried about?
opts: Losing a bat before the game
A broken strap on a glove
why: The dark clouds and the word rain show she fears the weather will stop the game.
hint: Connect the clouds to what the coach said.

q: A caption is the short line of words under a photograph or drawing. True or false: a caption explains what the picture shows.
why: Captions give details about a picture, like who or what is in it.
hint: Think about the words that sit next to a photo.

q: Octopuses squirt dark ink when frightened. The ink makes a cloud in the water, and the octopus swims away. Why does an octopus squirt ink?
why: The ink cloud hides the octopus so it can get away from a hungry predator.
hint: What happens after the cloud forms?

q: A comet is a ball of ice and dust. Near the Sun it heats up and grows a glowing tail. Which sentence tells the main idea?
opts: Comets are made of nothing but rock
Comets grow tails near the Sun
Comets stay far away from the Sun
why: Both sentences tell how a comet grows a tail near the Sun. Comets hold ice and dust, not just rock.
hint: Which choice covers both sentences?

q: Read: Rex has 5 books about sharks and 4 books about dinosaurs. He gives 3 books away. How many books does Rex have left?
why: 5 plus 4 makes 9 books. After giving 3 away, 9 minus 3 leaves 6.
hint: Add first, then subtract.

q: Every day after practice, Lena stays late to pick up balls, stack the bats and sweep the dugout, even when nobody asks. Which word best describes Lena?
why: Doing extra jobs without being asked shows she is helpful, not lazy.
hint: What do her actions show about her?

q: I felt my heart pound as I walked to the mound to pitch. Who is telling this story?
opts: A reporter watching from far away
why: The word I shows the storyteller is the person in the story, the pitcher.
hint: Which word shows who is speaking?

q: Put the water cycle in order.
opts: The Sun warms water in the ocean.
Water vapor rises into the sky.
The vapor cools and forms clouds.
Rain falls back to the ground.
why: Water must warm and rise before it can cool into clouds and fall.
hint: Rain cannot fall until clouds have formed.

q: Maya tiptoed into the kitchen at midnight and opened the fridge as quietly as she could. Why was she tiptoeing?
why: Midnight and 'as quietly as she could' show she did not want to wake anyone.
hint: Why do people move quietly at midnight?

q: Sharks and rays both have skeletons made of cartilage. A shark's body is shaped like a torpedo, but a ray's body is flat. What do sharks and rays share?
why: The passage says both have cartilage skeletons. Only rays have flat bodies.
hint: Find the thing the first sentence says they share.

q: Ice cubes melt faster in sunshine because the Sun gives off heat. True or false: ice cubes melt faster in a cool, shady spot than in the sunshine.
why: The Sun's heat melts ice faster, so a shady spot slows the melting.
hint: Which place has more heat from the Sun?

q: Which sentence would an author write to persuade you?
opts: An aquarium has many large tanks.
Many fish live in the tanks.
why: Should tells you what to do. The other sentences only give facts.
hint: Which sentence tries to change your mind?

q: The bats flew out of the cave at dusk, just as the sky was turning dark. What does dusk mean?
why: The sky was turning dark, so dusk is the time when day ends and evening begins.
hint: When does the sky start to turn dark?

q: Read: The team scored 2 runs in the first inning, none in the second and 3 runs in the third. How many runs did it score in the first three innings?
why: 2 plus 0 plus 3 equals 5 runs.
hint: Remember that none means zero.

q: The wind bent the palm trees almost flat, and waves crashed over the pier. What kind of weather was it?
why: Bending trees and crashing waves are signs of strong wind, like a storm.
hint: What would make trees bend and waves crash?

q: Unlike toothy sharks, baleen whales have no teeth. They filter tiny food from the water with bristly plates in their mouths. What do baleen whales use instead of teeth?
why: The passage says bristly plates in their mouths strain food from the water.
hint: Find the word instead in the question.

q: Put Ravi's pitching routine in order.
opts: Then he faced the first batter.
Finally, he struck the batter out.
why: Signal words like first, next, then and finally show the order.
hint: Look for the signal words.

q: At first, Omar was afraid to put his face in the water. After weeks of practice, he swam across the pool and grinned. How did Omar change?
why: He went from afraid at first to grinning after he succeeded.
hint: Compare how he acts at the start and the end.

q: Penguins huddle close together in cold winds. They take turns standing on the outside. That way no penguin stays in the coldest spot for long. What is the main idea?
why: All the sentences describe penguins taking turns in the cold. Nothing mentions homes or caves.
hint: What do all three sentences describe?

q: Which sentence contains a simile?
opts: The pitcher threw the ball very hard.
The ball sailed over the fence.
why: A simile compares two things using like or as. 'Like lightning' compares the fastball to lightning.
hint: Look for the word like or as.

q: The ocean waves whispered secrets to the sleepy shore. What is the author doing?
opts: Using the word like or as
Telling a plain fact about water
Giving an order to the reader
why: Waves cannot whisper or tell secrets. Giving human actions to nature is personification.
hint: Can waves really whisper?

q: When the ocean gets too warm, coral pushes out the tiny algae living inside it, and the coral turns white. True or false: the algae are what turn the coral white.
why: Losing the algae turns the coral white. The algae give coral its color.
hint: Read the order of events carefully.

q: The new student told a joke to break the ice with her classmates. What does break the ice mean?
why: Breaking the ice means making an awkward start feel friendly and comfortable.
hint: Think about why someone tells a joke to new classmates.

q: Mia practiced her curveball every day. She missed the strike zone for weeks but kept trying. By spring, she struck out three batters. What lesson does the story teach?
why: Her struggles turned into success because she kept practicing. That is the lesson of the story.
hint: Ask what changed from the start to the end.

q: Read: A pitcher threw 15 pitches in the first inning, 12 in the second and 18 in the third. How many pitches did he throw in all?
why: 15 plus 12 makes 27, and 27 plus 18 makes 45.
hint: Add the three numbers one at a time.

q: Lila read about space for hours. Every night she watched the stars and drew maps of the planets. Which sentence is best supported by these clues?
opts: Lila is afraid of the dark.
Lila wants to be a baker.
why: Reading, stargazing and drawing planets all show strong interest in space. Nothing hints at fear.
hint: Which choice matches ALL of her actions?

q: Put the bat's hunting steps in order.
opts: The bat makes a high squeak.
The sound hits a moth and bounces back.
The bat swoops to catch the moth.
why: Echoes come after the squeak, and the bat can only swoop once it hears the echo.
hint: What does the bat need before it can find the moth?

q: Tiny plant-like plankton need sunlight to grow, so they float near the ocean's surface. What would happen to them in the dark deep sea?
why: Without sunlight they cannot make food, so they could not grow well. That is why they stay near the top.
hint: What do they need to grow?

q: In the sentence 'Many sharks hunt fish; however, whale sharks eat plankton,' what does the word however signal?
why: However shows a difference: many sharks hunt fish, but whale sharks eat plankton.
hint: Does the second part match or differ from the first?

q: The Moon has no wind or rain to wipe away footprints, so astronaut boot prints can last a very long time. True or false: footprints on the Moon disappear quickly because of strong winds.
why: The Moon has no wind, so footprints stay. That is why they can last a very long time.
hint: Check what the text says about wind.

q: The reef was teeming with fish. They darted through every crack and crowded around every coral. What does teeming mean?
why: Fish in every crack and crowding around coral shows the reef was packed with life.
hint: What do darting and crowding tell you?

q: In a science book, a word printed in bold type usually means what?
opts: It is a key word to learn
It is the end of a chapter
why: Authors use bold type to point out important words, which are often explained nearby.
hint: Why would an author make a word stand out?

q: Read: A shark swam 4 miles before lunch. After lunch it swam twice as far. How many miles did it swim all day?
why: Twice as far as 4 miles is 8 miles. Add the 4 miles from the morning to get 12.
hint: Find the afternoon distance first.

q: After striking out, Kai slammed down his glove and stomped to the dugout. A minute later he picked it up and cheered for the next batter. What does this show about Kai?
why: Kai got upset but calmed down fast and cheered for a teammate. That shows he can recover.
hint: Compare Kai's actions before and after the minute passed.

q: Mars is dry, dusty and cold. Venus is wrapped in thick clouds and is extremely hot. How are the two planets different?
opts: Mars is hot and Venus is cold
Mars is cold and Venus is hot
why: Mars is described as cold and Venus as extremely hot. The other choices do not match the text.
hint: Match each planet to its temperature word.

q: Put the steps of how a pearl forms in order.
opts: A tiny grain slips inside an oyster.
The oyster coats the grain with smooth layers.
Layer after layer builds up over time.
A shiny pearl is ready to be found.
why: The grain comes first, and the layers must build up before the pearl is finished.
hint: What starts the whole process?

q: Pip called the game a thrilling comeback. Cam, who plays for the other team, called it a heartbreaking loss. Why do they feel so differently?
opts: One of them missed the game
why: A comeback for one team is a loss for the other, so their points of view differ.
hint: Which team does each person root for?

q: Herbivores eat plants and carnivores eat meat. The prefix omni- means 'all.' What do omnivores eat?
why: Omni- means all, so omnivores eat all kinds of food, both plants and meat.
hint: What does 'all' tell you about their food?

q: A summary tells only the most important ideas of a text in a few sentences. True or false: a good summary includes every tiny detail.
why: A summary keeps the big ideas and leaves out small details.
hint: Think about how short a summary should be.

q: The library was a quiet garden where stories grew. What does this metaphor suggest about the library?
why: A garden is peaceful and things grow there, so the library is calm and ideas grow. It is not a real garden.
hint: What do gardens and libraries have in common?

q: Ruben said his sister was too small to play. When the ball rolled under a fence, only she fit through to get it. Ruben grinned and handed her a glove. What is the theme?
why: The small sister helped in a way nobody else could. The theme is about value in everyone.
hint: Ask what Ruben learned by the end.

q: Read: A museum shows 3 dinosaur skeletons in each of its 4 rooms. It also shows 5 skeletons in the lobby. How many skeletons are on display?
why: 3 skeletons in each of 4 rooms is 12. Add the 5 in the lobby to get 17.
hint: Multiply first, then add the lobby.

q: A scientist left a cup of sea water in the sun for three days. The cup was almost empty, with white crystals on the bottom. What happened?
opts: It evaporated and left salt behind
It froze solid and cracked the cup
It soaked through the table slowly
why: Water evaporates into the air, but salt does not. It is left behind as crystals.
hint: Which part of sea water can float away as vapor?

q: Plastic bags were tangling sea turtles' flippers. A beach town asked shoppers to use cloth bags instead, and soon fewer turtles were hurt. Which text structure does this passage use?
why: It names a problem (tangled turtles) and a solution (cloth bags).
hint: Find the trouble, then find the fix.

q: Octopuses can squeeze through tiny gaps. Their bodies have no bones, so only the hard beak limits how small a gap they can fit through. True or false: the second sentence explains the first.
why: The second sentence gives the reason octopuses fit through tiny gaps: no bones.
hint: Ask whether the second sentence tells why.

q: Writer A says the new ballpark has narrow seats and long lines. Writer B says the seats are close to the action and the snacks arrive fast. What is the best conclusion?
why: A lists problems and B lists good things, so they have different opinions.
hint: Is each writer positive or negative?

q: A paragraph explains how bats use sound to find food. Which sentence does NOT belong?
opts: Echoes tell bats where insects are.
Bats listen for the returning sound.
why: Where bats sleep is a different topic than how they find food with sound.
hint: Which sentence is off topic?

q: Put these feelings in order from mildest to most intense.
why: Each word is stronger than the one before it, ending with the most intense, furious.
hint: Which word fits a tiny problem, and which a huge one?

q: Dani told her team she was not nervous. But her foot tapped, she checked her watch every minute and she kept retying her cleats. What can the reader infer?
opts: She is angry at her cleats
why: Her actions say the opposite of her words, so she is likely hiding nervousness.
hint: Compare what she says with what she does.

q: Warm seas let plankton bloom. The plankton drew small fish, and the small fish drew seabirds. What directly drew the seabirds?
why: The passage says the small fish drew the seabirds. Warm water and plankton were earlier links.
hint: Find the link right before the seabirds.

q: Baby sea turtles crawl toward the brightest horizon, which is normally the moonlit sea. Bright lights on land can confuse them. True or false: bright lights near a beach always help hatchlings reach the sea.
why: Lights on land can pull hatchlings the wrong way, away from the sea.
hint: Read the second sentence closely.

q: The paleontologist was meticulous. She brushed each tiny grain of dust off the bone, one grain at a time. What does meticulous mean?
why: Brushing off one grain at a time shows she is extremely careful.
hint: What does going one grain at a time show?

q: Hummingbirds beat their wings so fast that they hover. They sip nectar with long tongues. They burn so much energy that they must eat often. Which is the best summary?
why: A good summary covers the key ideas: hovering, sipping nectar and eating often.
hint: Pick the choice that uses ideas from all three sentences.

q: Read: A poem has 3 stanzas. Each stanza has 4 lines, and every line has 6 words. How many words are in the poem?
why: 3 stanzas of 4 lines is 12 lines. 12 lines of 6 words each is 72 words.
hint: First find the total number of lines.

q: The coach called the runner's plan 'bold.' The umpire called the same plan 'reckless.' How do the two words differ?
opts: They mean exactly the same thing
why: Bold praises daring, while reckless warns that it is careless. The feelings are different.
hint: Think of whether each word sounds like praise or worry.

q: At noon the boat sat on dry sand. Six hours later it floated at the dock. True or false: the tide probably came in.
why: A rising tide fills the shore with water, lifting boats that were sitting on dry sand.
hint: What would lift a boat off dry sand?

q: Text A: The Sun gives Earth light and heat. Text B: Without the Sun's heat, Earth's oceans would freeze. What idea do both texts share?
why: Both texts show things on Earth need the Sun's light and heat.
hint: Look for what both texts say about the Sun.

q: An anemone's stinging tentacles keep a clownfish safe. The clownfish cleans the anemone and chases away fish that nibble it. How would you describe this partnership?
why: Each helps the other: the anemone protects, and the clownfish cleans and guards.
hint: Ask what each one gets.

q: The old pitcher's fastball, once feared by every hitter, now barely reached the plate. True or false: the pitcher has probably lost speed over the years.
why: Once feared and now barely reaching the plate suggest he used to throw faster.
hint: Compare then and now.

q: Which situation is ironic?
opts: A swim coach who loves pizza
A swim coach who wears a watch
A swim coach who cannot swim
A swim coach who is very tall
why: Irony is the opposite of what you expect. A swim coach is expected to know how to swim.
hint: Which choice is the opposite of what you would expect?

q: Claim: sharks help keep the ocean healthy. Which fact best supports this claim?
opts: They eat weak fish, so others thrive
Their teeth grow back in many rows
Some sharks are gray and some are blue
Many sharks can swim at high speed
why: Evidence must connect to the claim. Only the first fact explains how sharks help the ocean's health.
hint: Which fact is about HEALTH, not looks or speed?

q: Read: A research boat sailed 3 days to a reef, stayed twice as many days as it sailed, then sailed home in 3 days. How many days did the whole trip take?
why: Twice 3 days is 6 days at the reef. The trip was 3 plus 6 plus 3, which is 12 days.
hint: Find the days at the reef first.

q: Had the tide not turned, the stranded whale calf would have stayed trapped on the sand. What happened?
opts: The tide never came back in
It was never stranded at all
It stayed trapped on the sand
It was freed by the tide
why: Had the tide not turned means it did turn. So the calf did not stay trapped.
hint: Say the sentence again as what really happened.

q: The forecast was dire, yet the captain stayed sanguine and smiled at her crew. What does sanguine most likely mean?
why: The word yet signals a contrast with dire, so she stayed hopeful and smiling.
hint: What does the word yet tell you?

q: Scientists say sharks were swimming in the oceans over 400 million years ago, before the first forests grew on land. True or false: sharks were around before the first forests.
why: The passage says sharks swam before forests grew. Sharks are very ancient animals.
hint: Compare the two time clues in the sentence.

q: When the runner wanted to risk stealing second, the coach said, 'A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.' What advice is she giving?
opts: Do not risk a sure thing
why: This saying means a sure thing is worth more than a bigger chance you might lose.
hint: What is the coach telling the runner not to risk?

q: Report A says the home team 'squeaked past' its rival. Report B says it 'crushed' its rival. Which report suggests a close game?
why: Squeaked past means barely won. Crushed means won by a lot.
hint: Which word means a tiny margin?

q: Put these sentences in order to make a clear paragraph.
opts: Sea otters are clever tool users.
For example, they crack clams open with rocks.
Some even keep a favorite rock in a skin pocket.
So tool use is not only for people.
why: A topic sentence opens, examples follow, and a sentence beginning with So wraps it up.
hint: Which sentence introduces the topic and which one concludes?

q: Most of an octopus's nerve cells are in its arms, not its head. Which inference is best supported?
why: With most nerve cells in the arms, each arm can handle some tasks itself. But the head still has a brain.
hint: Where would you expect a lot of nerve cells to help?

q: The graceful shark glided past the reef, where more than a hundred kinds of fish live. Which word shows the author's opinion?
why: Graceful is a judgment someone could disagree with. The other words can be checked.
hint: Which word could two people disagree about?

q: Nina ate four fish tacos and loved each one. She said, 'All fish tacos are delicious.' True or false: four tacos prove her statement about all fish tacos.
why: A small sample cannot prove something about all fish tacos. Her statement is an overgeneralization.
hint: Does four tacos cover every taco in the world?

q: The Sharks won 7 of their 10 games. The Comets won 6 of their 8 games. Which team won a greater share of its games?
why: 7 of 10 is 70 percent, but 6 of 8 is 75 percent. More wins does not mean a bigger share.
hint: Compare the shares, not the number of wins.

q: Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth. So when you see the Sun, you see it as it was about how long ago?
why: Light takes time to travel, so the sunlight reaching you left the Sun about eight minutes earlier.
hint: Light needs time to cross space.

q: Read: Each row at the ballpark holds exactly 12 fans. A school group of 50 fans arrives. What is the fewest number of rows that can seat all 50?
why: Four rows seat only 48 fans. The last 2 fans need a fifth row.
hint: Divide, then decide what to do with the leftover.

q: An article opens: 'What if you could hear a shark's heartbeat?' Why would an author begin with a question?
why: An opening question makes readers curious so they keep reading.
hint: Think about how the first line affects the reader.

q: Two books are called 'Parts of a Shark' and 'Why Every Beach Should Protect Sharks.' True or false: the title 'Parts of a Shark' suggests the author wants to persuade readers.
why: Parts of a Shark sounds like information. The word Should in the other title signals persuasion.
hint: Which title tells readers what they should do?

q: The umpire saw the runner leave the base early but turned a blind eye. What did the umpire do?
why: Turning a blind eye is an idiom meaning to ignore something on purpose.
hint: Is the umpire's eyesight the point here?

q: Most sharks live in warm water, but a few species thrive in cold seas. True or false: at least one kind of shark lives in cold water.
why: A few species thrive in cold seas, so at least one kind lives in cold water.
hint: What does a few species tell you?

q: The Greek root chrono means 'time,' and -logy means 'study.' A chronology is a list of events arranged by what?
why: Chrono means time, so a chronology lists events in the order they happened.
hint: Use the meaning of the root chrono.
